# How to sync your Airbnb calendar with Vrbo and Booking.com


by


[Guesty Marketing Team](https://www.guesty.com/blog/author/guesty-marketing-team/)

Share


Share


If you log into three different apps to close out dates every time a booking comes in, you are racing a ticking clock. A guest books on Airbnb, giving you minutes to block those dates on Vrbo and Booking.com before someone else grabs them. One slip creates a double booking, a forced cancellation, and a permanent hit to your search ranking. You need an automated system, and this guide shows you exactly how to[sync your Airbnb calendar with Vrbo](https://www.guesty.com/blog/sync-airbnb-calendar-with-vrbo-calendar/) and Booking.com.


**TL;DR**


- Double bookings trigger immediate cancellation penalties, lost revenue, and damaged search rankings on major booking platforms.
- iCal exports offer a free way to link calendars, but they carry dangerous update delays.
- A true two-way sync requires importing and exporting links across every single platform combination.
- Real-time API connections replace delayed iCal pulls with instant availability updates.
- A vacation rental software like Guesty® synchronizes your calendars across the top platforms automatically, so you never manually block a date again.


## The financial risk of manual calendar updates


Operating across multiple online travel agencies creates massive exposure if your calendars do not communicate. When a guest reserves a weekend on one platform, those same dates remain open on all other platforms until a system updates them. Manual updates demand constant vigilance. You fall asleep, and a booking slips through.


A double booking directly damages your business.


A guest books your weekend on Airbnb, and another guest finds the same dates open on Booking.com to complete checkout. You now have two confirmed reservations for a single property.


You must cancel one of these reservations, and the consequences hit immediately. Airbnb strips[Superhost status](https://www.guesty.com/blog/how-to-earn-and-maintain-superhost-status/) from hosts who cancel confirmed reservations. Booking.com forces you to pay the difference to relocate the canceled guest to a similar property. Both platforms penalize your listing in their search algorithms, pushing your property down the page where future guests never see it.


Protect your profit margins and search visibility by connecting your calendars. The platforms provide built-in tools to share availability data, which you just need to configure correctly.


## How to sync calendars manually using iCal


The most basic synchronization method uses iCal links, a universal calendar standard ending in “.ics”. Every major booking platform generates a unique iCal link for your property.


You take the link from one platform and paste it into another. The receiving platform reads the link and blocks off dates that already have reservations.


You must establish a two-way sync, as a one-way sync only pushes data out. If you only paste your Airbnb link into Vrbo, Vrbo knows about Airbnb bookings, but Airbnb remains completely blind to your Vrbo bookings. You must import and export on every platform.


### Step 1: Export your Airbnb calendar


Log into your Airbnb host dashboard. Navigate to your listings page and select the specific property you want to sync. Click on Pricing and Availability. Scroll down to the Calendar Sync section. Click Export Calendar. Airbnb generates a unique URL, which you need to copy to your clipboard.


### Step 2: Import your Airbnb calendar to Vrbo


Open your Vrbo host dashboard in a new tab. Navigate to your calendar view. Click the Import/Export icon. Select Import Calendar. Paste the Airbnb URL into the designated field. Assign a clear name like “Airbnb Sync” to identify the source. Save the connection. Vrbo now reads your Airbnb calendar.


### Step 3: Import your Airbnb calendar to Booking.com


Log into your Booking.com Extranet. Click on Rates & Availability. Select Sync Calendars. Click the Add Calendar Connection button. Paste the Airbnb link. Name the connection. Click Next to finalize the setup. Booking.com now blocks dates reserved on Airbnb.

### Step 4: Complete the two-way sync across all channels


You established a one-way connection from Airbnb to your other channels, and now you must reverse the process. Export your Vrbo calendar link. Import it into Airbnb. Import it into Booking.com. Export your Booking.com link. Import it into Airbnb. Import it into Vrbo. You must map every possible combination, because skipping one link leaves a gap open for double bookings.


## The hidden risks of iCal syncing


The iCal method costs nothing to set up, but it carries a massive operational flaw by being incredibly slow.


Platforms do not push iCal updates instantly. They pull data at scheduled intervals. Airbnb might pull data from Vrbo every two hours, while Booking.com might pull data every six hours. If a guest books on Vrbo, those dates remain open and bookable on Airbnb until the next scheduled pull.


You might assume a two-hour sync window is fast enough for everyday operations. During flash sales or peak holiday booking seasons, that two-hour gap leaves your property wide open for overlapping reservations.


This latency creates a massive blind spot. You still face the exact same double-booking risks you tried to avoid. Furthermore, iCal links frequently break. A platform runs an update, the link drops, and you receive no notification. Your calendars quietly stop syncing while you assume everything works perfectly.


## Real-time API channel managers


Professional hosts do not rely on delayed iCal links, opting instead for API connections. An Application Programming Interface creates a direct, real-time software bridge between your core system and the booking channels.


[API connections](https://www.guesty.com/features/api/) push data instantly. When a guest books your property on Booking.com, the API connection tells Airbnb, Vrbo, and Expedia to block the dates immediately. The delay disappears, eliminating the risk.


API connections sync multiple data points simultaneously. While iCal links only transfer blocked or open status, an API connection synchronizes your nightly rates, minimum stay requirements, and seasonal rules across every channel. You update your weekend rate once, and the API pushes the new price everywhere.
